prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 218px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 147px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 1235px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 62px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 599px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 598px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [140, 88, 82, 205, 83] · table 599×918px · row heights [33, 174, 134, 134, 134, 154, 154] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [165, 82, 78, 190, 83] · table 599×978px · row heights [33, 194, 154, 134, 134, 154, 174] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [130, 80, 80, 225, 83] · table 599×857px · row heights [33, 154, 134, 134, 134, 134, 134] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [145, 75, 75, 220, 83] · table 599×857px · row heights [33, 154, 134, 134, 134, 134, 134] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [125, 85, 85, 220, 83] · table 599×857px · row heights [33, 154, 134, 134, 134, 134, 134] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [165, 80, 75, 195, 83] · table 599×938px · row heights [33, 174, 154, 134, 134, 154, 154] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [175, 78, 70, 192, 83] · table 599×978px · row heights [33, 194, 154, 134, 134, 154, 174] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [160, 90, 70, 195, 83] · table 599×938px · row heights [33, 174, 154, 134, 134, 154, 154] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r2A"],"acceptable":["r2B","r2C","r1B"],"bad":[{"design":"r3B","why":"Gives the widest treatment to the shortest column (course name 175px) while squeezing the description to 192px (171px of text) and the trainer to 70px (49px of text); the description — by far the heaviest column at 1235px unwrapped — forces 9-line cells and a 978px-tall table, and trainer names like «م. عبدالله الشمري» break into an ugly two-line stub."},{"design":"r1C","why":"Same inversion of emphasis: 165px to the name column against 190px for the description, producing the tallest rendering (978px) and 9-line description cells; the reader pays a full screen of scrolling for a row header that only ever needs two lines."}],"contrast":{"widths":[119,119,119,119,122],"why":"Equal widths treat every column as equally important: the description collapses to ~98px of text and runs 14+ lines, the table becomes absurdly tall, while «الرسوم» and «المدة» get acres of white space around three- or four-character facts. Plausible as a 'fair' grid, wrong as an information hierarchy."},"ranges":[[122,142],[74,88],[74,88],[212,232],[83,86]],"rationale":"The table is a catalogue: the reader first identifies a course by its name (right), then checks duration, trainer and fee, and only optionally reads the long description.
